host.name: zbook
host.gpu: AMD Radeon 8060S (gfx1151, Ryzen AI MAX+ 395, 40 CU, unified LPDDR5X)
host.rocm: 7.15.26333 / hipBLASLt from the same ROCm SDK
host.note: Every figure is gfx1151. No gfx1100 hardware was available.

change.what: The YuE2 AR and NAR runtimes selected their hipBLASLt algorithm as the first zero-workspace candidate hipBLASLt returned. They now use HipblasLtProblem.fast_algorithm(), a fixed index into that same filtered list (FAST_ALGORITHM_INDEX = 4), which is the index the wrapper's own convenience selector already documented as the measured gfx1151 fast heuristic.
change.why: hipBLASLt returns candidates in its own heuristic order, not by measured time, and its first entry is 1.4-5.7x slower than the measured best on these shapes.
change.reproducibility: A fixed index, not a runtime autotune, so two runs of the same input select the same algorithm and stay comparable run to run.

shape_results_other_rows.rows_1: all candidates within 15% (best index 5/6/6/3, every one under 0.5 ms)
shape_results_other_rows.rows_64: index 4 best on three of four shapes (1.47-2.93x), index 0 best by 0% on the fourth

algorithm_scan.summary: Across 16 shapes, index 4 is fastest in 11 and within 15% of fastest in the rest.

solver_effect.method: hipengine.runtime.yue2_nar.Yue2NarRuntime._gemm wrapped with a device synchronize on either side, over the same solve used for the attention split

ar_replay_gate.note: The 'before' row is benchmarks/results/yue2_ar_replay_hipblaslt_20260916.json. The 18 cases were not re-run against the strict arm in this session, so the 522.5 s strict figure is cross-session; only the batched route's own 91.3 s -> 77.6 s is same-protocol.

solver_gates_after_change.reading: The production arithmetic moved slightly, as a different GEMM accumulation order must. Every gate stays inside its calibrated envelope; the multi-chunk case reproduces its recorded numbers exactly.

session_gate_after_change.note: Every case improved slightly; all pass.

next_candidates: NAR attention is again the solver's dominant per-evaluation cost at the product's 32 steps (about 53 s of the 81 s solve): the tile maximum is still a serial 128-entry shared-memory walk per row per tile, and fmax is order-independent so a warp shuffle keeps it exact.
VAE decode is 20.1 s of the 28.0 s two-step replay and 20.1 s of the 101.2 s thirty-two-step replay.
The AR decode path (576 steps of the 77.6 s replay) still runs on GEMV kernels and was not touched by this change.
